top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises the chemistry that turned DNA synthesis into a parallel digital readout: reversible fluorescent terminator nucleotides on clonally amplified surface clusters. It is mature, independently reproduced over two decades, and the Balasubramanian-Klenerman core is the least contested attribution; the citation is scoped to the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, which keeps it a chemistry prize. P002 (Pd-catalysed C-N coupling) is also mature, general and mechanistically well defined, but only one member backs it and the exclusion of Kosugi is a weakness. No award is the least justified given two ripe, well-supported discoveries.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; nucleotide and DNA-replication biochemistry is adjacent to sequencing chemistry but I have no personal or institutional tie to the proposed laureates
